action.prompt:
You are an expert in Conventional Commits and Git best practices.

Perform the following steps IN ORDER. Stop immediately if any step fails and report the error.

## Step 1 — Check for staged or unstaged changes
Run: git status

If the output shows "nothing to commit, working tree clean", stop here — there is nothing to commit.

## Step 2 — Stage all changes
Run: git add .

## Step 3 — Inspect the staged diff
Run: git diff --staged

Analyze every changed file carefully. Identify:
- Which layer was modified (controller, service, domain, infra, config, test, docs)
- The primary intent of the change (new feature, bug fix, refactor, test, docs, chore)
- The scope (module name: consumo, auth, perfil, recompensa, sesion, websocket, config, etc.)

## Step 4 — Generate the commit message

Apply Conventional Commits format strictly:

```
<type>(<scope>): <short summary>

Why: <one sentence explaining the reason for the change>
What: <one sentence describing what was changed>
```

Rules:
- First line: maximum 72 characters, imperative mood, no period at end
- Type must be one of: feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs, test, perf, build
- Scope: lowercase module name (omit if change spans many modules)
- No emojis
- Why/What body lines are mandatory

Examples of good first lines:
- feat(consumo): add endpoint to register healthy food intake
- fix(recompensa): prevent duplicate reward on concurrent requests
- chore(config): add Flyway migration V1 for usuarios table
- test(perfil): add WebMvcTest for PerfilController create endpoint
- refactor(auth): extract token validation to dedicated TokenService

## Step 5 — Create the commit
Run: git commit -m "<first line>" -m "Why: <why>" -m "What: <what>"

Report the full commit message used and confirm the commit was created successfully.
